summary.text: Marine life is the living species of the sea: over 242,000 had been documented by 2023, and perhaps two million more are still undescribed.
Life began in the oceans, which by volume still provide about 90% of the living space on Earth.
Sea algae and cyanobacteria make oxygen and lock away carbon through photosynthesis, enough to shape the chemistry of the atmosphere.

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: From 0.02-micrometre plankton to 33 m blue whales

facts.label: Microbes' share
facts.value: Estimated at about 70% or 90% of marine biomass

items.prompt: Add up all the space on Earth where living things can live, measured by volume. Roughly what share is ocean?
items.explain: By volume the oceans provide about 90% of Earth's living space; 71% is only the share of the surface they cover.

items.prompt: Early in Earth's history, a huge rise in oxygen changed ocean chemistry. Which living things were hit hardest?
items.explain: The Great Oxygenation Event likely caused a widespread extinction of anaerobes, organisms that live without oxygen.

items.prompt: A stretch of coastal water suddenly loses most of its dissolved oxygen. Which animals are most likely to die off in large numbers?
items.explain: Marine vertebrates such as fish need a lot of oxygen and suffer mass deaths in low-oxygen events, while invertebrates cope far better.

items.prompt: If you could weigh every living thing in the sea, which group would make up most of the total?
items.explain: Marine microorganisms are estimated to make up about 70% or about 90% of all marine biomass.

items.prompt: A low island in a warm sea sits on rock that living animals built up over a long time. Which animals most likely made it?
items.explain: Some marine organisms, such as corals, help create new land as their reef-building material accumulates.

items.prompt: Some fish hatch in rivers, grow up at sea, then swim back upriver. What does this kind of travel do for ecosystems?

options.label: It keeps rivers free of all other fish
It makes seawater less salty over time
It carries biomass and energy between regions
It stops algae from growing in the sea

items.explain: Migratory species such as anadromous fish move biomass and biological energy between different regions of Earth.

beats.title: Life Started Out Wet
beats.hook: Long before anything grew on land, life was taking shape around vents on the deep sea floor.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the early history of ocean life in order.

items.label: Simple microbes appear around deep-sea hydrothermal vents
The Great Oxygenation Event changes ocean chemistry
The Avalon Explosion of mostly fixed-in-place animals
The Cambrian Explosion of actively moving animals

beats.explain: The first microbes arose in Archean oceans, oxygen rose in the early Proterozoic, the Avalon Explosion came in the Neoproterozoic, and the Cambrian Explosion followed in the early Phanerozoic.

beats.prompt: Oxygen floods the ancient oceans, where the existing microbes live without it. What happens next?
beats.explain: The Great Oxygenation Event likely caused a widespread anaerobe extinction, but it also led to eukaryotes through symbiogenesis between surviving anaerobes and aerobes.

choices.label: Many die out, but survivors team up into a new kind of cell
All life in the sea is wiped out for good
choices.feedback: Tempting given the scale of the shock, but some anaerobes survived and went on to form new life.

choices.label: Nothing changes, since microbes ignore oxygen
choices.feedback: Tempting because microbes are tough, but the change in chemistry was severe enough to likely cause a widespread extinction.

beats.prompt: Match each kind of sea life to what it is known for.

right.label: Can be as small as 0.02 micrometres
Help create new land by building reefs

beats.explain: Marine life spans an enormous size range, and some groups reshape the planet itself, from the air to the land.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong; which?

steps.text: Marine vertebrates include saltwater fish, marine mammals, marine reptiles and seabirds.
Vertebrates tend to be active swimmers with high oxygen needs.
Marine invertebrates need even more oxygen than vertebrates do.
So when oxygen runs low, fish are among the first to die in large numbers.

beats.explain: Marine invertebrates are much more tolerant of low oxygen than vertebrates, with many adaptations for poorly oxygenated water.

beats.idea: Life began in the oceans, spread from there into fresh water and onto land, and sea life still shapes the air and the shores.
